nodes.name: NPG CVD synthesis
nodes.procedure: NF was washed with ethanol and deionized water to remove organic substance and oxide layers. Subsequently, the treated NF as template was warmed to 950 °C in an Ar atmosphere. Then, methane (CH4) and ammonia (NH3) as carbon and nitrogen sources, respectively, in high-temperature reducing atmosphere (950 °C, H2/Ar), underwent cracking reactions and uniformly deposited on the NF template. Finally, NF template was etched with 1.0 mol·L-1 FeCl3/HCl solution at 80 °C, then FeCl3/HCl solution was removed thoroughly with deionized water.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal MoCo-LDH synthesis
nodes.procedure: NPG substrate was placed in the 70 ml homogeneous aqueous solution containing Na2MoO4·2H2O, Co(NO3)2·6H2O, NH4F (6 mmol) and urea (10 mmol). In the above solution, the total amount of metal ions was 3 mmol, and various Mo/Co molar ratios were attempted, such as 0:10, 1:9, 2:8, 3:7 and 4:6. MoCo-LDH grown on NPG substrate (MoCo-LDH@NPG) was obtained after reacting at 120 °C for 6 h.

nodes.name: Pt/C electrode preparation
nodes.procedure: 5 mg commercial Pt/C (10 wt%) powder and 40 μl Nafion solution were dispersed in 1 ml isopropanol solvent with the assistance of ultrasonication. The prepared homogeneous ink was dripped onto the surface of NPG in small amount and dried until the mass loading of Pt/C reached 0.65 mg·cm-2.

nodes.name: Mo0.3Co0.7@NPG
aliases: honeycomb-like porous MoCo alloy on NPG

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo0.3Co0.7@NPG exhibits honeycomb-like morphology composed of intersecting vertical nanosheets. Co@NPG shows flower cluster-like structure of nanowires ~3 μm long.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the morphology of Mo0.3Co0.7@NPG (Fig. 2j–l) emerges honeycomb-like morphology composed of a large number of intersecting vertical nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo0.3Co0.7 nanosheet maintains thickness of ~450 nm with uniformly distributed pores of average size 10 nm after annealing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Mo0.3Co0.7 (Fig. 3a) maintains the nanosheet with thickness of ~450 nm ... there are uniformly distributed holes with an average pore size of 10 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Clear lattice fringes with interplanar spacing of ~0.179 nm (slightly larger than Co(200) plane 0.177 nm) and ~0.195 nm belonging to Co3Mo(201) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM image of Mo0.3Co0.7 (Fig. 3b) exhibits clear lattice fringes with interplanar spacing of ~0.179 nm ... The interplanar spacing of ~0.195 nm (Fig. 3c) belongs to (201) plane for Co3Mo.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co and Mo are evenly distributed on the surface of Mo0.3Co0.7 nanosheet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS mapping images (Fig. 3d–f) show that Co and Mo are evenly distributed on the surface of the Mo0.3Co0.7 nanosheet.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo0.3Co0.7 composition is 34 at% Mo and 66 at% Co.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP further shows that the proportion of Mo and Co is 34 at% and 66 at%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Main diffraction peaks at 44.1°, 51.0° and 75.7° correspond to Co(111), (200) and (220) planes. Peaks shift to lower angles with increasing Mo content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: main characteristic diffraction peaks of different alloys (Fig. S4a) at 44.1°, 51.0° and 75.7° reflex the (111), (200) and (220) crystal planes of Co ... diffraction peaks of MoCo alloys shift gradually to low diffraction angle with the increase in Mo.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p peaks at 778.4/794.8 eV (Co⁰), 783.2/798.5 eV (Co²⁺), 781.2/797.0 eV (Co³⁺). Mo 3d peak at 227.7 eV (Mo⁰), confirming MoCo alloy formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co 2p spectrum of Mo0.3Co0.7@NPG (Fig. 3g) presents three different valence states, the peaks at 778.4 and 794.8 eV are characteristic peaks of Co⁰ 2p3/2 and Co⁰ 2p1/2 ... According to XPS of Co and Mo, the Co⁰ and Mo⁰ show the formation of MoCo alloy.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo0.3Co0.7@NPG exhibits largest Cdl of 5.5 mF·cm⁻², indicating highest ECSA among MoCo@NPG samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Mo0.3Co0.7@NPG exhibits the largest Cdl (5.5 mF·cm⁻²) ... which is much larger than that of Co@NPG (3.1 mF·cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo0.3Co0.7@NPG shows Rs of 3.83 Ω and Rct of 0.23 Ω, smaller Rct than Co@NPG (0.68 Ω).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Rs of Mo0.3Co0.7@NPG and Co@NPG are 3.83 and 3.08 Ω ... Mo0.3Co0.7@NPG has smaller Rct (0.23 Ω) than Co@NPG (0.68 Ω).
